questions.q: If $A=\frac{1}{3}\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ a & 2 & b\end{array}\right]$ is an orthogonal matrix, then
questions.solution:
We know that, if A$ is an orthogonal matrix, then
\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \quad \ AA^T=I \\
\Rightarrow \\
\Rightarrow \quad\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 2 \\
2 & 1 & -2 \\
a & 2 & b
\end{array}\right] \cdot \frac{1}{3}\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & a \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
2 & -2 & b
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{lll}
1 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 1
\end{array}\right] \\
\Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 2 \\
2 & 1 & -2 \\
a & 2 & b
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & a \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
2 & -2 & b
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{lll}
9 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 9 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 9
\end{array}\right] \\
\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
9 & 0 & a+4+2 b \\
0+4+2 b & 9 & 2 a+2-2 b \\
2 a+2-2 b & a^2+4+b^2
\end{array}\right] \\
\quad=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
9 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 9 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 9
\end{array}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \quad a+4+2 b=0 \text{ and } 2 a+2-2 b=0 \\
a+2 b=-4 \ldots(i)\\
a-b=-1 \ldots(ii)
\end{gathered}$
By solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$a=-2, b=-1$

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{array}\right], P=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$ and $X=A P A^T$, then $A^T X^{50} A=$
questions.solution:
Since $A A^T=I$ therefore matrix $A$ is orthogonal matrix.
Now, $A^T X^{50} A=A^T X^{49}\left(A P A^T\right) A=A^T X^{49} A P\left(A^T A\right)=A^T X^{49} A P=A^T X^{48}\left(A P A^T\right) A P=A^T X^{48} A P^2 \ldots \ldots$.
$=A^T A P^{50}=I P^{50}=P^{50}\because \quad P=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \Rightarrow P^2=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\Rightarrow P^3=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \ldots.$.
$\Rightarrow \quad P^{50}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 50 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$
So, $A^T X^{50} A=P^{50}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 50 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$

Given,& $P = \left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right]$

$∴ P^{T} = \left[\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right]$

Also given~$P^{T}P = I$

or~$\left|\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right|2 = 1 ⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{cases}\right| = \pm 1$

questions.q: The value of \(\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{3-3 x^2}\right)\); \(\frac{1}{2} \leq x \leq 1\) is
questions.solution:
Let \(\cos ^{-1} x=y\)
\(\Rightarrow x=\cos y\), so that \(\frac{1}{2} \leq x \leq 1\) or \(\quad 0 \leq y \leq \frac{\pi}{3}\)
and \(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{3-3 x^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cos y+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin y\)
\(=\cos \frac{\pi}{3} \cos y+\sin \frac{\pi}{3} \sin y=\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3}-y\right)\)
\(\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{3-3 x^2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}-y\)
\(\therefore\) the given expression is equal to
\(y+\frac{\pi}{3}-y, \text{ i.e., } \frac{\pi}{3}\)
